title: Ordinary compact-support quotient cocycle
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and $f:X\to Y$ compactifiable, separated, quasi-compact and locally of finite type between Noetherian schemes. The actual ordinary compact-support coefficient maps of [def-pur-finite-smooth-coefficient-arrows], on the chosen compactification, satisfy ExceptionalCoefficients.CompactSupportCocycle for every $r\ge m\ge n\ge1$, with both canonical scalar associators. This is a conclusion, not an additional assumed cocycle.

source.place: Part (2), compact-support coefficient cocycle used in the exceptional transpose calculation.

proof.text: Reuse the derived restriction/pullback coefficient-chain identity and conjugateEquiv_paste to prove the inverse open coefficient cocycle. Invert the equality of the two composites of open isomorphisms to obtain the forward open cocycle. Reuse finiteCoefficientDirectImageMap_coefficientChain and its proved equality with scalarMate for the direct-image cocycle. Expand compactSupportMap, apply the proper cocycle, then the open cocycle, and use naturality of scalarMate to paste them. Specialize to the actual quotient maps by their explicitly proved composition equality.

proof_origin.place: K1 proof via existing private scalarRestriction_chain, conjugateEquiv_paste, and the existing direct-image coefficient-chain theorem.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteSmoothCompactQuotientCocycle
    (ell : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [HasCompactification f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    ExceptionalCoefficients.CompactSupportCocycle ell f
